proposals.relationship: Ouellet challenges Creighton’s national-bourgeoisie and social-decapitation account of the Conquest while identifying shared assumptions with later Quebec nationalist interpretations.
proposals.evidence_note: Own 1984 survey 226–228 explicitly places Creighton before Séguin in connecting the Conquest with removal of a commercial bourgeoisie, then questions that class’s autonomy and its supposed harmony with the colonial metropolis. Ouellet proposes an Ancien Régime society dominated by military/landed nobility and clergy, and treats commercial dependence differently. He preserves differences among Creighton, Séguin, Frégault and Brunet, not an identical doctrine. At 228 he acknowledges revising his own earlier near-total social-continuity account concerning the Conquest’s negative political and military effects on the nobility; 229 credits Creighton among economic-social pioneers. This scoped disagreement coexists with Ouellet and Hamelin’s separate 1962 borrowing in edge 991. Original Creighton books and the other historians’ cited works remain unread.
primary_locators: Original RHAF 38:2 (1984), selected printed 223–229 and notes 1–20, especially 226–228; critical 227–228 visually collated.

proposals.relationship: Davis contrasts Creighton’s emphasis on metropolitan elites with Careless’s ecological interdependence and questions the latter’s combination of elite agency with impersonal systems.
proposals.evidence_note: Named scholarly reader Davis 1985:97–98 and 101–103 distinguishes several metropolitan approaches rather than one thesis. His comparison identifies Creighton’s entrepreneurship of central elites and Careless’s mutually dependent city–hinterland relations; it also criticizes Careless’s uneven combination of Laurentian elites with Gras’s ecological model. Crucially, at 101 and note 47 on 110 he reports Careless’s explicit denial that his original inspiration came from Creighton or Innis, crediting medieval communitas studies and Gras instead. The undirected comparison therefore records Davis’s interpretation, not a proved teacher–pupil lineage, personal endorsement or contradiction resolved in favor of one author. Careless’s cited private letter and original works remain unread.
primary_locators: Actual original Davis 1985 PDF, printed 97–98 and 101–103; note 47 at 110 identifies quoted private letter. Selected 95–99 also read.
